finalJustifications: Because the origin of Security Group is dynamic and maintenance zero: any instance associated with the application SG — current or future — achieves the 3306; the rest of the VPC, no.
Because the rule by SG converts application instance IPs into a static list managed by AWS, updated by deployee.
Because the SG rule creates a dedicated tunnel between the two private sub-networks, isolating the door 3306 of the rest of the internal network.
Because the rule by SG delegates authentication to IAM of the instances, and each MySQL connection is validated by the role of the origin instance.

finalJustifications: Because the endpoints keep everything in the network of AWS: PrivateLink interface for the SSM and gateway endpoint for the S3 — the sub-network follows without NAT and no internet.
Because endpoints copy configuration files and commands from SSM within the VPC, served locally without external calls.
Because the endpoints open a temporary exception in isolation only during each call of API, closed at the end of reply.
Because the endpoints use the management connection of their own AWS (outside the VPC), same as the hypervisor uses for the console.

finalJustifications: Because the roll in Account A with trust policy for Account B allows sts:AssumeRole: auditors receive TEMPORARY credentials only reading, no long-term key.
Because the trust policy replicates Account B users as reading identities in Account A, synchronized to each audit done.
Because AssumeRole transfers the roll to Account B during the audit, returning it to Account A at the end of each usage session.
Because the role demands that Account B be in the same organization, and it's the Organizations authenticating auditors between accounts.

finalJustifications: Because GuardDuty analyze CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs and DNS with ML and thread intel — malicious IPs, anonymous APIs, log sabotage — with severe detections, no agents.
Because GuardDuty automatically blocks detected C&C IPs, containing the incident even before the finding is generated.
Because GuardDuty installs temporary sensors in the instances during the analysis, removed at the end of each daily count scan.
Because GuardDuty audit permissions IAM of the roles and disables the credentials used outside the usual region of each user.

finalJustifications: Because the supported route is this: instance snapshot → snapshot copy with KMS enabled → restore in a new encrypted instance → redirect the application endpoint.
Because the encrypted copy of the snapshot converts the original instance in-place in the next window, without needing any restorative.
Because encrypted snapshot synchronizes with the old instance in continuous replication, allowing the exchange without perceptible downtime.
Because the restare only applies encryption to new data, and the history is gradually encrypted by the bank's subsequent writings.

finalJustifications: Because Deny with condition denies anything that doesn't come from VPC Endpoint (aws:SourceVpce) and corporate IPs (aws:SourceIp) — Even valid credentials outside the source are barred.
Because the conditional Deny revokes permissions IAM of identities that try to access from outside, punishing invalid origin in time.
Because the condition aws:SourceVpce encrypts endpoint traffic, and only the origins with the key can read financial reports.
Because politics with Deny moves the bucket into the VPC, making it unattainable for any route outside the corporate network.

finalJustifications: Because Session Manager gives shell via agent SSM with permissions IAM: no door 22, without keys, without bastion — and with centrally recorded sessions for audit.
Because Session Manager keeps an invisible managed bastion inside the AWS, that makes the bridge SSH without cost or team management.
Because Session Manager converts keys SSH in short-term certificates issued by the IAM every new session started.
'Cause Session Manager tunes the SSH corporate API of AWS, maintaining the protocol and eliminating only the door exposure.
